thesis: LeBron James at age 40 displayed contradictory performance signals in late 2024/early 2025: record-breaking individual milestones contrasted with analysis suggesting diminished efficiency and team performance decline when he played.

facts.claim: In December 2024, The Ringer reported Lakers performed better when LeBron rested than when he played, a reversal of his career pattern.
LeBron set the NBA record for career minutes in December 2024 while averaging 23 points, nine assists, and eight rebounds per game.
On January 3, 2025, LeBron broke Michael Jordan's record with his 563rd career 30-point game.
In February 2025 at age 40, LeBron became the oldest player to score 40 points in a game.
LeBron turned 40 years old on December 30, 2024, after spending over half his life in the NBA.
Erik Spoelstra noted in early December 2024 that LeBron remained mentally sharp and fully engaged in team preparation despite his age.

verified_numbers.context: Career 30-point games, breaking Michael Jordan's record on January 3, 2025

timeline.event: The Ringer analysis published questioning if age had caught up to LeBron, noting Lakers performed better in minutes he sat out.
LeBron James turned 40 years old; NBA.com celebrated his record career spans and sustained elite status.
LeBron recorded his 563rd career 30-point game against Atlanta Hawks, breaking Michael Jordan's record.
LeBron became oldest player to score 40 points in an NBA game at age 40.

topic: LeBron James’ age vs. elite performance debate (December 2024/January 2025)
